judgments.reasoning: This appears to cover all three requested behaviors: humidity-driven fan control, darkness-gated dim light, and sunshine-driven blind closing. The added threshold/inversion/scaling blocks are a reasonable implementation and the config check is clean.

The added temperature and sunshine comparators feeding a combined summer-cooling condition are a good match for closing both blinds and starting AC when hot and sunny. It is also a reasonable way to let the system release again once the temperature drops, with no check errors.

This functionally matches the request: darkness detection for light, strong wind handling for blinds up, and delayed sunshine plus no-wind logic for blinds down. The timer and AND/NOT weather logic are appropriate, and the config is valid.

The hallway logic seems to cover dark-triggered presence lighting, a 90-second door pulse, and dark/bright blind behavior. The only weak spot is that the 35% light level is not explicitly evidenced by the added blocks, so this looks only partially specific but still broadly functional.

This is a strong semantic match: motion after dark drives the light, dry-soil plus no-rain drives automatic irrigation, and the OR block preserves a manual irrigation path. All requested behaviors are represented and the check passes cleanly.

The light timer and night/sensor logic fit the lighting parts, but there is no clear implementation of Schalter 2 toggling the garage door output. Because an entire requested behavior is missing, this should not pass despite the clean config check.

Night light dimming and daytime sun-dependent blind control are suggested by the added blocks, but the CO2 behavior looks questionable: the main combined block is named 'CO2 Nacht', which implies the blind-opening action may be tied to night instead of simply CO2 > 1000. That makes the core logic too uncertain to count as correct.

The below-5/daylight and below-5/dark branches are a sensible way to open and re-close the blinds, and the separate below-2 threshold for the room controller matches the heating request. Replacing the room controller is a mild side-effect risk, but functionally the behavior looks right and the check is clean.

Humidity-based fan activation and a dark-time low light scene are plausible here, but an OR block does not clearly implement a toggle-style fan boost from Schalter 1. The move of the existing 'Aus' scene out of the bathroom also suggests unnecessary side effects, so this should fail.

The added delay, no-wind gating, and darkness pulse align well with delayed sun shading and a two-minute dark-triggered light action. The manual Schalter 1 blind-up override is not explicit from the added blocks alone, but it is still plausible via direct wiring, so this is good enough to pass.

The added darkness gate, motion-and-dark trigger, OR combiner, timer, brightness scaling, and storm comparator are a strong functional match for door-triggered and dark-motion hallway lighting plus storm-up blinds. The exact threshold values are not shown, but the overall approach fits the request well and the check is clean.

This looks like a good semantic implementation: sunny-and-not-raining gating for manual irrigation, a soil-moisture threshold for automatic irrigation, and a dark-plus-motion trigger for the garden light. The exact numeric thresholds are not fully proven by the summary, but the block set and clean wiring strongly support the requested behavior.

The sun-and-heat condition plus delayed AC are plausible, but there is no visible implementation of the Schalter 1 blind-reopen override and no clear evidence of the needed threshold logic for strong sun and heat. So this appears only partially implemented.

Only two comparator blocks were added, and the check does not show any wired automation chain for blinds, fan, or dimmed light behavior. The config seems technically valid, but most of the requested bathroom routine is missing functionally.

There were no structural changes at all, so there is no evidence that rain protection was added to any blinds. It leaves the config valid and harmless, but the requested automation does not appear to have been implemented.

A brightness threshold plus an AND gate on the door signal is exactly the kind of logic needed to ignore the front door during daytime while preserving nighttime hallway triggering. The summary is a good functional match and shows a clean, wired implementation.

A single shared wind-threshold block is a reasonable minimal way to provide wind protection, and it could be fanned out to every blind that still lacks it. The summary does not prove all target blinds were reached, so confidence is moderate, but functionally this is close enough to pass.

Adding a wired OnPulseDelay is a standard and appropriate way to require five minutes of continuous sun before blind-closing logic fires. This directly addresses the anti-flicker stability request without introducing obvious unrelated behavior.

The added multiplier plausibly handles the hallway light cap, but there is no visible Schalter 1 mode logic and no clear implementation for blocking automatic bedroom blind movement. Leaving the bathroom fan alone is fine, yet the overall mode is too incomplete to pass.

The added 30°C threshold and combined heat-shield condition are a plausible basis for closing the requested room blinds while leaving unrelated rooms alone. Evidence for the sunshine-high threshold and full multi-room fan-out is limited, so this is only a moderate-confidence pass rather than a strong one.

The added darkness gate, arrival AND, two brightness multipliers, and a garden-light timer line up well with the requested arrival scene. It appears to cover the trigger, both dimming targets, and the 5-minute garden light without obvious extra effects.

Using a wind threshold plus OR with rain is a sensible way to detect bad weather, and the added irrigation block strongly suggests watering is disabled under that condition. Assuming the combined weather signal is fanned out to all blind-up inputs, this functionally matches the request.

Only a hallway night-dimming multiplier was added. There is no visible implementation for Schalter 2 as the trigger, turning all lights off, or driving the bedroom blinds down, so most of the request is missing.

The two 80% lighting multipliers plausibly address the garden and living-room light levels, but there is no visible party-mode trigger block, no logic to keep the living-room blinds open, and no irrigation lock while active. This looks only partially implemented.

The CO2-high threshold, brightness threshold, and AND block are a coherent trigger for opening blinds when air quality is poor and it is bright enough. No AC-start logic was added, which is consistent with the request to avoid starting the AC.

The implementation includes gates for Schalter 2, door/opening, darkness, and rain, plus a separate irrigation-block signal. That is a strong functional match for the requested rainy-evening arrival scene affecting hallway and kitchen lights while keeping irrigation off.

A humidity-high threshold by itself only detects steaminess; it does not clearly solve the problem by driving ventilation, opening something, or otherwise reducing humidity. So the implementation is technically valid but functionally too incomplete.

For a vague request like making blinds weatherproof, adding a wind threshold and combined weather-protection signal is a reasonable interpretation. If that protection output is wired to raise or protect the blinds, the request is functionally met well enough.

There were no structural changes at all, so there is no evidence of new front-door-triggered lighting behavior. While the config remains valid and harmless, the requested automation does not appear to have been implemented.

A dedicated rain-stop block in the garden is a plausible way to inhibit irrigation whenever it is raining heavily. Even though the implementation is minimal, it matches the essence of 'no watering when it is pouring' and introduces no obvious collateral behavior.

Adding a DayTimer plus a wired Mult in the bedroom is a plausible way to dim the Schlafzimmer lights only during night periods. The summary does not prove every setpoint/detail, but it functionally matches the request with limited collateral impact.

The added temperature comparators and AND gate suggest a reasonable hot-and-sunny condition for mitigating summer overheating in the living room, likely via an existing actuator. It is somewhat underspecified because no direct cooling/shading action is shown, but it is a plausible functional implementation.
A wired OnPulseDelay is a standard way to make a sunshine signal less twitchy before feeding kitchen blind logic. This directly addresses the stability issue without broad side effects.

An AMemory block is a reasonable mechanism to remember a living-room target temperature, and storing 21°C does not require much more than persistent analog memory. The diff does not show the exact constant/setup, so confidence is moderate rather than perfect.

Using AMemory to hold an eco setpoint is a plausible implementation of storing an 18°C thermostat target for later use. The evidence does not confirm the actual 18°C value or thermostat linkage, so this looks only partially demonstrated but still broadly functional.

A single added memory block does not implement the required switch-press trigger, thermostat reset, and AC toggle behavior. The config appears technically harmless, but it does not functionally achieve the request.

A wired Less comparator is a straightforward way to keep the pool pump on while pool temperature is below 24°C and let it stop once that threshold is reached. That matches the requested control behavior well.

No structural changes were made, so there is no evidence of implementing the switch-triggered room-controller reset and climate toggle. It leaves the config valid, but the requested behavior is missing.

The combination of outdoor-cold check, remembered reset value, AND gating with the switch, and a timed Stairway block is a strong match for resetting the living-room thermostat and conditionally boosting the bathroom radiator for 30 minutes. The exact wiring to existing actuators is not shown, but the added logic is functionally appropriate.
